summary: The department has changed its internal regulations on the publication requirements for graduate degree conferral, applying to students examined from the second semester of the 2026 academic year (September 2026). The notice also sets detailed criteria under which abstract-only conference papers may be recognised.
applies_to: All graduate students (Master's, Doctoral and Integrated Master's-Doctoral programmes) subject to thesis examination from the second semester of the 2026 academic year (from September 2026) onwards.

steps: Read the Academic Handbook (학사안내서) together with this notice; all other degree conferral requirements not covered here remain unchanged and must still be met.

Ensure your publication record meets the requirement for your programme (Master's, or Doctoral/Integrated), with your supervisor included as a co-author and your name listed first among the authors other than your supervisor.

Obtain proof of publication or acceptance (e.g. publication record, acceptance email) that can be issued before the submission date for thesis examination result documents in your examination semester.

If you are using an abstract-only conference paper, confirm the conference has a peer-review process, obtain the signature (confirmation) of a preliminary examination committee member for that paper, and submit it before the submission date for thesis examination result documents. Title: Notice of Changes to Graduate Degree Conferral Regulations (Thesis-Related) for Master's, Doctoral and Integrated Master's-Doctoral Programmes
Posted: 29 August 2026

We hereby announce the changes to the internal regulations on degree conferral (thesis-related) for all graduate programmes (Master's, Doctoral and Integrated Master's-Doctoral), as set out below. (Decided by the Academic Committee on Thursday, 26 February 2026 / detailed criteria added by the Academic Committee on Monday, 10 August 2026.)

Effective date: From September 2026 (from students subject to examination in the second semester of the 2026 academic year).

The following is an excerpt of the thesis-related regulations in the Academic Handbook [학사안내서]. All other degree conferral requirements not listed here remain unchanged and must be met as before. Please be sure to check the Academic Handbook as well.

1. Publication Requirements for Degree Conferral

A. Master's
Publication (or confirmed acceptance) of at least one domestic or international conference paper or one journal paper in which your name is listed first among the authors, excluding your supervisor. However, your supervisor must be included as a co-author of the paper.
- Documents proving submission to a journal will not be accepted even if submitted (the previous guideline recognising them is abolished).
- Even if your name is listed first, the paper will not be recognised if you are a co-first author.

B. Doctoral and Integrated Master's-Doctoral
Both Item 1 and Item 2 below must be satisfied. Only papers or patents in which your supervisor is included as a co-author and your name is listed first among the authors, excluding your supervisor, will be recognised.
- (Item 1) Publication or confirmed acceptance of at least one paper in an internationally recognised journal (SCI(E) level).
- (Item 2) Publication or confirmed acceptance of at least one international conference paper or one domestic journal paper, or at least one registered international patent.

C. Supporting Documents (common to Master's and Doctoral)
Documents proving publication or confirmed acceptance (publication record, acceptance email, etc.) must be documents that can be issued before the submission date for thesis examination result documents in the examination semester. Documents issued after the result document submission date will not be recognised as achievements.

2. Detailed Criteria for Recognising Conference Achievements

Conferences requiring submission of an abstract only
Conferences that require only an abstract, rather than a full paper, may also be recognised if the following requirements are met.

- Recognition criterion: The conference must have a peer-review process.
- Verification method: Obtain the signature (confirmation) of a preliminary examination committee member for the achievement and submit it.
- Submission deadline: Submit before the submission date for thesis examination result documents.

The signature may be obtained after the preliminary examination, provided it is submitted within the above deadline.

The acceptance rate is not applied as a recognition criterion.

3. Important Notes

The detailed criteria in Section 2 above were newly established by the Academic Committee on 10 August 2026. If any areas requiring improvement are identified during operation, revisions may be announced through this post after review by the department office.

For any ambiguous points or matters that are difficult to judge, please be sure to contact the department office before submitting your achievements.

The exact regulations and the final decision on whether requirements are met (recognised) are subject to the judgement (criteria) of your department. Please note in advance that, even if you meet the above, there may be cases in which the requirements are not recognised depending on detailed regulations or individual circumstances.

4. Please Also Check

Graduate School essential information: https://ece.snu.ac.kr/community/academics?md=v&bbsidx=56747
Thesis examination information: https://ece.snu.ac.kr/community/academics?md=v&bbsidx=56884
List of conferences recognised as equivalent to international journals (SCI(E) level) for doctoral degree requirements: https://ece.snu.ac.kr/community/academics?md=v&bbsidx=52081
Information on co-first authorship: https://ece.snu.ac.kr/community/academics?md=v&bbsidx=55998

Inquiries: Please send an email to the staff member at the department office; replies are given in order of receipt. (The contact details are in the original notice.)
